`Error on line 14: >>>On<<< AliasSym Expected` - ours rejects (SL-V034). `On`/`Off` are readable wherever a boolean is expected, which is why reads stay exempt from SL-V019, but they are reserved words and may never be declared. At the declaration position the tool wanted an alias and found the reserved word instead. Implemented as a **validation** rule over the variable-declaration family (locals, module parameters, record fields) plus DATATYPE names. `GroupData` is deliberately untouched: it is a reserved *type*, not a runtime constant, and we intentionally accept it as a type name.

Error on line 35 SEQTRANSITION TrStart WAIT_FOR>>>(*<<<. Expression expected. - ours rejects. The grammar used to say `seqtransition: SEQTRANSITION NAME? WAIT_FOR comments? expression`, i.e. it explicitly invited a comment between `WAIT_FOR` and the expression. That clause was backwards and has been removed; the comment must now sit *between* sequence elements, which `sequence_body` still allows. This was a **reversal**, not a missing rule - and the fixture that asserted the old behaviour, `edge_cases/CommentInsideEquation.s`, had the comment "inline comment is stripped" baked into it. No AST change was needed.

Error on line 15 >>>(*<<< AliasSym Expected - ours rejects. The grammar used to let `variable_list` accept a `comments` alternative alongside `variable_group`, the only place a bare comment was admitted as a declaration-list item. Everywhere else comments are `code_comment` and live inside *code* lists (entercode / activecode / exitcode / equationblock / sequence_body / if_statement), so that opt-in was the anomaly. Removed: a comment cannot be an item in a variable list, and it cannot sit before `LOCALVARIABLES` either. Note this probe's stated subject is duration-literal formats, which the real tool **never reached** - it died on this comment at line 15. So it is evidence about comment placement and says nothing yet about the duration forms.
